finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can inject malicious input into the input file that causes atoi to parse a string that represents a number larger than the maximum value for an int, leading to undefined behavior.
finding.assumptions: The input file is untrusted and can be controlled by an attacker. The atoi function is used to parse the number of threads, which could be manipulated to cause overflow.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported sink is atoi(line.param_one), which merely converts a string to an integer and does not invoke any OS command execution function. Therefore the claim of OS Command Injection (CWE‑78) is incorrect. While atoi can overflow on very large inputs, this results in undefined behavior rather than command injection. No checks or sanitization are present, but the vulnerability type is misidentified.
